newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton show gains on hike in state prices.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton show gains on hike in state prices.

text.p: Indian cotton prices on Friday rose owing to a hike in the selling prices of state-owned agencies, dealers said.
Though the progress of the monsoon has brightened prospects for new crops, heavy rain in some areas has compelled farmers towards a second sowing which may delay the start of new season.
In spot deals Bengal-deshi rose by 20/25 rupees to 1,050/1,070 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) and Punjab saw-ginned by 10/15 rupees to 1,825/1,875 rupees per maund.
Gujarat cotton was quiet in a limited activity. State-owned Maharashtra Cotton Growers' Federation had hiked selling prices by 200/300 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) on Thursday.
